instruction:
Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to create a Verilog module that implements a programmable ROM (read-only memory) block. 
A ROM block is a type of memory circuit that allows data to be read from it but not written to it. 
There are several types of ROM blocks, including mask ROM, programmable ROM, EPROM, EEPROM, and Flash, each with different features and capabilities.
Your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: a set of n address signals (addr1, addr2, ..., addrn)
Outputs: a set of m data signals (data1, data2, ..., datam)
The module should also have the following parameters:

n: the number of address signals
m: the number of data signals
w: the width of each data signal (in bits)
t: the type of ROM block (mask ROM, programmable ROM, EPROM, EEPROM, or Flash)
Your module should implement the following functionality:

The circuit should have a memory array that stores a predetermined set of data values.
The circuit should read the data values from the memory array in response to the input address signals.
The memory array should be configured according to the type of ROM block specified by the t parameter.
To implement the ROM block, you should use Verilog code to define the memory array and to initialize it with the predetermined set of data values. 
You should then use the input address signals to select the appropriate data value from the memory array and output it on the data signals.
You should also implement the logic required to configure the memory array based on the specified ROM block type.
